Under this new framework, celebrities can promote brands, but they’re prohibited from making specific endorsements about products. Any ad featuring a celebrity must receive approval from Sebi or a recognized supervisory authority beforehand.

items.title: Mahindra begins commercial rollout of MaxSeeder to tackle stubble burning
items.summary: Mahindra & Mahindra has initiated commercial production of its new multi-crop seeding machine called Maxseeder. This machine is designed to sow various crops, like rice, wheat, and cotton, efficiently. It operates using lower-horsepower tractors, making advanced seeding technology more accessible for farmers. Additionally, the Maxseeder promotes sustainable farming by eliminating the need for stubble burning.

items.summary: Indian rice exporters have partnered with Eximwala Solutions to utilise bulk shipping for their products with an aim to significantly lower freight costs by about 74%, enhancing competitiveness. The shipments will mainly target the Gulf region, where demand for Basmati rice is substantial.

items.title: India shields city gas users as Hormuz crisis threatens South Asia's LNG demand
items.summary: India has shielded city gas supplies from Middle East LNG disruptions by cutting deliveries to fertiliser plants, refineries and industrial users, helping it weather the crisis better than Pakistan and Bangladesh, Wood Mackenzie said. Even so, India has faced sharply higher LNG prices and an estimated 1.5 million-tonne reduction in gas demand, as the regional supply shock reverses earlier expectations for South Asian LNG growth.

items.title: Noida’s new Sports City plan approved: Authority tells SC 70% of land will be reserved for sports facilities as stalled Sector 150 project moves towards revival
items.summary: Noida Authority has approved the revised layout plan for the 300-acre Sports City project in Sector 150, reserving 70% of the land for sports facilities. The approval follows years of stalled development and comes as the Supreme Court examines separate cases involving Sports City projects. While four housing projects have received conditional occupancy certificates, further approvals and legal proceedings will determine the next steps for construction and homebuyers awaiting possession.

items.title: Elara initiates coverage on Adani Power, sees up to 17% upside as expansion plans gather pace
items.summary: Elara Securities has initiated coverage on Adani Power with an Accumulate rating and a target price of Rs 220, implying 17% upside. The brokerage expects capacity expansion from 18.3 GW to around 42 GW by FY32 to drive growth, while flagging execution risks, rising debt and limited valuation headroom.

items.title: India's retail inflation quickens to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, hits near two-year high
items.summary: India's retail inflation accelerated to 5.54% in September 2026, a notable rise from August's 4.83%. This jump is particularly linked to rising food prices, predominantly in vegetables. Rural inflation hit 6.08%, outpacing urban inflation at 4.88%. In response, the Reserve Bank of India increased the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points on October 7, 2026, and revised its inflation outlook for the fiscal year 2027.

items.title: RBI measures, intervention spark rupee's sharpest rally in six months
items.summary: On Monday, the Indian rupee gained about 1% after the Reserve Bank of India announced measures to curb dollar demand. Oil companies' dollar purchases will now be directed away from the spot market, easing pressure on the rupee. This intervention aims to address the mounting balance of payments challenges due to high oil prices. However, analysts remain cautious about the sustainability of the rupee's recovery moving forward.

The brokerage sees the stock’s 22% correction from its peak as an opportunity, citing attractive valuations, rising power demand, improving utilisation at Khavda and expansion in battery storage.

items.summary: In a strategic push, GE Aerospace plans to ramp up its supply chain spending in India, setting an ambitious goal of USD 400 million. This initiative emphasizes their commitment to the burgeoning Indian aviation market and supports local sourcing initiatives. Presently, GE partners with established suppliers like Tata Group and Mahindra, while also focusing on enhancing their technological and innovative proficiencies in the region.

The Integral Coach Factory in Chennai has been tasked with manufacturing 50 such trainsets. The development is part of a wider plan to introduce more than 200 Vande Bharat sleeper trains for long-distance overnight travel.

items.summary: India's recently unveiled India Semiconductor Mission phase 2 or ISM 2.0 which focuses on design and Intellectual Property (IP) creation, helping complete the value chain and making the country Atmanirbhar (self-reliant). The new phase is focused on producing semiconductor equipment and materials in India as well as designing full-stack semiconductor intellectual property. The Union Cabinet had also approved the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, aiming to boost private sector investment.

The Solicitor General emphasized the importance of maintaining a balance between drug availability and market dynamics in determining prices.

While high-speed corridors have expanded more than 12-fold, trucks in India still cover far less distance daily than those in the US and China. The government aims to develop around 51,000 km of high-speed corridors over the next decade to improve connectivity and freight movement.

items.title: Telecom stocks under fire, sink up to 13% as Elon Musk’s Starlink buys spectrum from Grain Management
items.summary: SpaceX’s move to acquire low-band spectrum licences has intensified concerns about disruption in the US telecom industry, sending shares of Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile lower. The company plans to combine satellite connectivity with terrestrial infrastructure to expand Starlink Mobile coverage. The deal, alongside regulatory approval for its next-generation satellite constellation, signals an escalation in SpaceX’s challenge to established wireless operators.

items.title: Blackouts hit Indian factories as coal crunch feeds into economy
items.summary: Indian industries and households are grappling with power shortages due to reduced coal supplies and extreme weather conditions. The weak monsoon has limited hydropower generation while demand for electricity has surged. Many factories, including small steel mills, are facing lengthy outages, impacting production and increasing costs. Consumers in states like Uttar Pradesh are experiencing significant blackouts, prompting investments in backup systems.

items.title: India wastes 1.8 billion units of renewable power amid shortages and dwindling coal stocks: Report
items.summary: In July and August, India faced significant curtailment of renewable electricity despite rising power demand. Nearly 1.8 billion units of electricity were turned away due to infrastructure challenges in absorption. Approximately 4.2% of total solar generation could not integrate into the grid during this period. Coal remains the primary electricity source, supplying two-thirds of total demand despite increases in renewable energy.

items.title: FIIs cut stakes in 12 stocks in September quarter; shares fall up to 27% in 3 months

items.title: India’s office hubs turn into retail hotspots as developers tap captive shoppers
items.summary: Office clusters in cities like Gurugram and Mumbai are increasingly becoming retail hubs that serve employees. Retail spaces within office developments have surged significantly, catering to rising consumer demand for lifestyle services. Developers are adapting to this shift by integrating retail areas into office structures. This evolution supports the needs of both workers during the week and consumers on weekends.

items.title: FII ownership hits 17-year low, but foreign holdings in Indian equities rise 3.6 times to $783 billion: Report
items.summary: Foreign investor ownership in Indian equities has fallen to a 17-year low of 15.1%, but the absolute value of holdings has risen to around $783 billion. OmniScience Capital attributes the decline in ownership share to faster growth in domestic investor participation.

items.title: Train stopped in nick of time: Forest staffer's quick thinking averted possible tragedy when elephant herd approached railway tracks; video wins hearts online
items.summary: A forest staffer, Akash Kerketta, helped save a herd of elephants in West Bengal by waving a red flag to alert an approaching Sikkim Mahananda train on the Bagdogra–Naxalbari route. The train pilots responded in time, preventing a possible accident. An IFS officer's post on X praising Kerketta's quick action has won appreciation online, with users calling him an unsung hero.

items.title: US Market: Four warning signs that bond selling could intensify

items.title: India’s monsoon risks may raise food industry costs: D&B
items.summary: India is experiencing agricultural risks attributed to monsoon conditions, which could impact food processors and poultry producers. Procurement costs and inventory needs are likely to rise significantly due to these agricultural challenges. Rice and wheat stocks provide immediate buffers against potential food-supply issues, but maize faces direct risks from production shortfalls. Affected states include Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, which contribute significantly to overall foodgrain output.

Mittal's long-standing relations with France began at Airtel's inception in 1992 with Compagnie Générale des Eaux. items.title: RBI tightens rules for forex bets to shield bruised rupee
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has tightened regulations on foreign exchange derivatives to stabilize the rupee's value. A special window will cater to the daily dollar needs of specific oil marketing companies. These actions aim to reduce speculative dollar demand and enhance market discipline. Bankers suggest these measures could impact the rupee's market value and trading activity.
